found_values.value: 5.5 V and 8.4 V are nominal set points; the highest voltage at a port's supply pin is the F16 ceiling, 6.0 V (LV) and 8.7 V (HV). SLVSI72A gives VOUT_FULL 9.85 to 10.15 V on the 10 V range (VOUT_FS 01h, REF 0780h) and VREF 1.117 to 1.141 V at 1.129 V, 0.837 to 0.855 V at 0.846 V, 0.501 to 0.514 V at 0.508 V; with those, 5.5 V gives 5.40 to 5.59 V and 8.4 V gives 8.27 to 8.53 V (FU-2B2's derivation, which its P4 re-derived as 5.41 to 5.59 V and 8.27 to 8.53 V). Ripple and load-step overshoot depend on round 2's capacitors and are not included. Applied as 'Set point against the ceilings'

An output of the main coprocessor's I/O expander, with a pull-down that holds EN/UVLO below VEN_L 0.4 V while that output is an input (IOBoard.md Measurement coprocessor reset and Load gates at reset). A MODE resistor of 0 Ohm (75h) or 48.7 kOhm (74h) sets the default OE bit to 0 (Table 6-2). The rail's temperature latch (V283, V303) also holds EN/UVLO low: the two combine in an AND, whose part is not selected. Applied as 'Enable off at reset' and 'Temperature trip input'

33 lines on the main coprocessor's I2C bus: 20 port switch enables, 5 bias selectors, 5 converter enables (4 TPS55285 and the TPS55288), the hardware latch read-back, and 2 inputs (DC input source status and brownout). GPA7 and GPB7 of the MCP23017 are output only and carry none of these, so 14 usable lines a part and 3 parts. The port supply switch topology of this run uses the same 20 enable lines (the INA301's RESET is tied to its port's enable) and adds none. Applied as 'Lines'

400 kHz: the only I2C rate in the tree is SET_I2C_KHZ, 100 to 400 kHz in 100 kHz steps, default 400. The TPS55285 takes 100 to 1000 kHz, the MCP23017 up to 1.7 MHz, the MCP9808 up to 400 kHz. Applied as 'I2C clock'

found_values.value: Yes. The servo rail gate is R3's one high-side switch on each servo rail and on the adjustable supply's output, open within 5 ms of the enable node falling; the 20 port supply switches are driven through the I/O expander and are not the gate. Applied as 'Not the rail gate'
3.0 A continuous, the per-servo current ceiling at which the procedures abort at once; it applies from a rail of 5.0 V up (V282). Applied as 'Continuous current'

Yes: each port limits its own current, with its whole tolerance band between 3.0 A and 6.35 A: at or above 3.0 A the firmware abort acts first, and under 6.35 A, the rail's limit, one shorted port does not pull the other ports into the converter's limit. The specification names a port breaker of 3.96 to 4.84 A (IOBoard.md:113). Applied as 'Own current limit'

570 mV across the switch path at 3.0 A from a rail of 5.0 V up; below 5.0 V the drop is reported (V282). Basis: the LV setting's low edge 5.40 V (V114) against the lowest operating voltage of the low-voltage servo read, 4.8 V (Savox SH-0255MG+: 'Operating Voltage (V) 4.8V - 6.0V'), 0.60 V, less 30 mV in the 10 mOhm port shunt. Applied as 'Voltage drop'

Under 5 mA at 8.4 V: an open port leaks less than the idle current of the lightest load read, 5 mA ('Quiescent Current (mA) 5' for the SH-0255MG+ and the SB-2290SG); the same 5 mA placeholder as the servo rail gate (IOBoard.md:218). Applied as 'Off-state leakage'

Yes, with the pin up to 12 V, while the switch is on and while it is off: an ESC on a port drives its BEC onto the port's supply pin, and YGE's BEC 'is adjustable from 5.5V to 8.4V, with the Saphir series up to 12V'. Applied as 'Reverse blocking'

5 ms from an RP2354B reset to every port switch open: the specification's opening time for a power switch (servo rail gate, 5 ms from the enable node falling), inside V1's 500 ms stop deadline. Applied as 'Opening time after reset'

LV: may cut off from 5.59 V, must cut off by 6.00 V. HV: may cut off from 8.53 V, must cut off by 8.70 V. The lower edges are the highest set points of V114, the upper edges F16. The HV band is +/-0.99 % about 8.615 V, the LV band +/-3.5 % about 5.795 V. Ripple and overshoot are not included. Applied as 'LV trip band' and 'HV trip band'
found_values.source: F16 Answer (Research.md); IOBoard.md:386 (checkout bb10544e89be); V114 above

found_values.value: Not found: no source read gives a time a servo survives above its rating or a cut-off time for the ceiling. The Savox pages give operating ranges only (4.8 to 6.0 V, 6.0 to 8.4 V); docs/OpenYGE.md:253 states only that a BEC value above the servos' rating damages them. Recorded, not a pass or fail limit

8.4 V, 2 x 4.2 V a cell (IOBoard.md Pack voltage range, owner 2026-09-30). The SLS XTRON vendor page states no charge voltage, so 4.2 V a cell is not confirmed by the vendor. Applied as the top of 'Pack input range'

In boost the pack current is the inductor current: 5.59 A at 6.0 V at the 3.72 A continuous rating; in overload ILIM_AVG bounds it, 7 A min, 8 A typ, no maximum stated, so no maximum rules out a clamp above 9.9 A. Applied as 'Pack current at 6.0 V'

Peak inrush at most 2.35 A from the rail: the rail's 6.35 A setting less the 4.0 A a synchronised pair may draw on other ports (docs/Servo.md:68-69). The capacitance a port presents is not found: no servo or receiver page read gives one. Applied as 'Inrush'

6.35 A as the TPS55285 output current limit setting, enabled at reset, with OCP_DELAY 00b = 128 us at reset; hiccup off time 76 ms. It is a setting, not a bound: no tolerance is given at 6.35 A, and during the delay only ILIM_AVG (7 A min, 8 A typ, no max) bounds the output. The port's own limit (V123) acts first on one shorted port. Applied as 'Current into a shorted port'

Cut-off state: yes, read from the port monitor's bus-voltage reading, which falls behind an open switch; with V130 the firmware reports the cut-off. Jumper position: no; the setup screen lists the ceilings as set in hardware. Applied as 'Cut-off state readable'

20 V: the TPS55285 programs up to 15 V, its output OVP trips at 110.5 to 120 % of the set point, VOUT is rated 17 V absolute maximum, and a converter failed through passes the DC input, 20 V at most (V112). Applied as 'Input withstand'

Each of the 20 port switches switches its port from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V; with V282 it turns on from 0.8 V and carries the port's current, the 3.0 A and 570 mV applying from 5.0 V up; with V302 the function may be split across parts (a switch from 0.5 V or below with separate reverse blocking, current limit and 20 V protection). TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V (SLVSFC9C 6.3, FU-2B2 reading 2026-10-02T14:00:46Z) and fails. A split topology passes: TLP3545A(TP1,F photorelay (C connection) + CMS04(TE12L,Q,M) Schottky + INA301A1IDGKR breaker. Applied as 'Operating input range' and 'Conducts from 0.8 V'

found_values.value: Each port is cut off above 6.0 V (LV) or 8.7 V (HV), set by a jumper (F16), with V128's bands; per V130 (owner, 2026-10-02) the port reconnects by itself once the rail falls below the ceiling, with the comparator's own hysteresis, no latch, and the firmware reports the cut-off. A cut-off below the band would cut a rail set from 0.8 V (V55), so the ceiling acts above the band only.
